title: Make Repo reads honor --branch (contents/append_lines are branch-blind)
desc: DEFECT (verified: cormac's finding 3, t-56ac; independent review #f0613640): Repo.contents (bin/chatcode:312) accepts a ref, but the call sites that matter for writes — append_lines at :409, update_task's contents() read, delete_file — pass none, so every read consults the DEFAULT branch while write_text/delete honor self.branch. On any -b branch: the first append to a fresh file creates it on the branch, the second re-reads the default branch, finds nothing, PUTs without sha -> 422 AlreadyExists retry loop -> dies with the misleading 'too many agents writing at once'. SCOPE: pass ref=self.branch (or thread an explicit ref) through the read paths used by write operations on the remote Repo; leave LocalRepo alone. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a test that fails on main and passes on the branch proving a second append to a fresh file on a non-default branch succeeds — mock or scratch-branch with cleanup, one command, output in PR body; (2) no behavior change on the default branch; (3) no format changes (R10). NON-GOALS: the >1 MB wipe (separate task t-20261011-0fc4), refactors.
